title: Wisdom Literature Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of Psalms, Proverbs, and Ecclesiastes — the Bible's wisdom books!

questions.question: According to Proverbs 9:10, what is the beginning of wisdom?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 9:10 says 'The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom.' True wisdom starts with respecting and honoring God.

questions.question: How many psalms are in the book of Psalms?
questions.explanation: The book of Psalms contains 150 individual psalms written by various authors over many centuries.

questions.question: In Psalm 23, what does David call God?
questions.explanation: David, who had been a shepherd himself, called God 'my shepherd' to show how God provides, protects, and guides His people.

questions.question: Who wrote most of the book of Proverbs?
questions.explanation: King Solomon, the wisest man who ever lived, wrote most of the book of Proverbs.

questions.question: What did Solomon ask God for when he became king?
questions.explanation: Solomon asked God for wisdom to lead His people, and God was so pleased that He also gave Solomon riches and honor (1 Kings 3:5-12).

questions.question: According to Proverbs 22:1, what is more desirable than great riches?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 22:1 says 'A good name is more desirable than great riches' — our character and reputation matter more than money.

questions.question: What is the main message of the book of Ecclesiastes?
options: True meaning is found only in God
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes concludes that without God, everything is meaningless. True purpose and meaning come from fearing God and keeping His commandments.

questions.question: Ecclesiastes 3:1 says there is a time for everything. What does this teach us?
options: God has a purpose for every season of life
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 3 teaches that God has appointed a purpose for every season — times of joy, sorrow, work, rest, and everything in between.
